title: The Kushymonster
author: Kush Kapoor
desc:
*Recommended for Intermediate lifters or above because of intensity techniques, but beginners are welcome to try.

This program is hypertrophy focused, built to target every major muscle group in your body for comprehensive muscle development and strength gains. As someone who’s tried a plethora of influencer-created programs, and tested my own, I’ve picked and chosen my favourite tips and tricks to put into this program. We’ll use intensity techniques, we’ll train to failure, and we’ll select exercises that maximise our focus on muscle stimulation (taking issues like stability, injury, etc. out of the equation).

We’ll train 3 on, 1 off. SARMS, Legs & Abs, Chest & Back, rest. Repeat.

Always control the eccentric, pause at the stretch, and explode up (safely). There’s no set tempo, but each rep should last at least 2 seconds.

Rest at least 90 seconds between all sets. Some will require more rest, and that’s okay.

I hate to use the word “optimal,” but this program is built to be optimal. We’ll run a 6-day, 10 week program, with a deload week after every 4 weeks (weeks 5 and 10). Exercise selection will be based on mine and my clients’ personal experience—how much you can feel the target muscle, how well you recover, and how much strength you can gain. From personal experience, as a lifter and personal trainer of 3+ years, a former fat person, and a former skinny guy, I really think anyone would enjoy this.

I hate the conception that you need to do 3 sets of every exercise. That’s not true. You can build muscle on 1 set, as long as you train intensely enough. Our priority in this program is INTENSITY; you’ll leave the gym feeling the right muscle every session—I promise. Follow my instructions and cues and you’ll feel yourself making progress. I find myself performing worse when I know I have to do 3 sets of everything; I push myself much more when I only do 2 sets. Because of our high volume, we’ll mainly do 2 sets of every exercise, but will train each day twice per week.

You may miss the standard heavy compound lifts, but we’ll incorporate those in variations (smith machine bench and squat, RDLs, dips and pull ups) to make strength gains as well as muscle gains. I tend to stay in the 6-15 rep range, but if you want to focus on strength in a certain compound lift, you’re welcome to reduce the reps and increase sets. Just make sure, above else: 

Train hard; recover harder.

Let’s get big(ger) together.

ex.note: Set cable just below wrist, use cuff, D-handle, etc. Take 2 steps to side (away from stack); lean in/firmly brace opposite arm against machine. Feel stretch in side delt; raise out and slightly front.

Press your back against the pad to make sure you’re not using your upper chest.

Add lengthened partials once you’ve reached failure on the second set (.#)
Set the cable around abs-height; step forward and lean so that the cable path travels smoothly above your torso. Use a triangle grip and stretch and extend fully, focusing on your triceps.
Set cables around ankle height and step back. Hinge at hips and bend knees so torso is roughly 45 degrees to the ground, then fly out and up, focusing on your delts, not traps. End with partial reps.

ss.note: Set cables at wrist height and take two steps forward, feeling stretch in biceps. Curl up and control the eccentric; once you reach failure, end with a 30 second static stretch.
Fix your arm at a 30 degree angle and lock your upper arm in place. Extend fully and IN LINE WITH ARM and control the eccentric; don’t move your upper arm to cheat.

ex.note: Set a cable at lowest height between your legs. Face away and raise till your arms are parallel to the ground; keep your arms straight.

ss.note: Brace against a bench, stretch fully at the bottom of each rep, and curl all the way up.
Keep your torso straight, brace against the cable, and ensure you’re locking out BEHIND your torso to target the long head of your tricep.

ex.note: Bottom half ONLY; control the weight down, stretch, and explode up. Never fully lock out
Lean forward to feel a stretch on your glutes
Lean forward to maximise stretch on hamstrings; finish with partials
Lean back on seat; end with partials
Bottom half only; feel stretch and roll ankles. End with 30 second static stretch
Feel ab stretch; manage breathing and exhale while curling

ss.note: Flat bench; emphasise stretch and end with partial reps. Wide grip
Integrated partials. Keep back in place to avoid using momentum and cheating. Fully stretch mid back at the bottom; row with arms at 60-90 degrees to target upper back. Wide grip.
Sit on 30-45 degree incline bench; focus on deep stretch. Don’t lock out
Control form; focus on mid and upper back. Shoulder width. Don’t use thumbs on grip. End with partials and a stretch
Low to high cable flies; slight bend in arms. Focus stretch upper chest
Integrated partials; stretch rear delts and upper back. Close/triangle grip; can use bar and landmine if no machine available
DEFICIT decline push-ups; control eccentric; pause at bottom. Shoulder width
Bottom half only; feel upper and mid back stretch and row controlled. Shoulder width. Go heavy

ex.note: Sit on a bench and set around 45 degree incline. Pronate hands so pinkies guide the movement; stretch delts fully at your sides and raise forwards and to the side (in a V shape). Finish with partials
Brace your torso so you don’t cheat with your chest. Lower to below chin, then explode up.
Brace against a 60 degree bench. Hammer curl up, supinate hands, and lower dumbbells mimicking the eccentric portion of a standard dumbbell bicep curl. Pronate hands at bottom to begin hammer curls
Start with a face pull; as you pull, rotate your arms up around the axis of your elbows, so you end with your arms above you in goalpost shape. Reverse this movement to lower.

ss.note: Don’t use momentum to swing the weight.
Straight bar; stretch fully and extend fully and slightly in front.
Close grip; do a tricep extension to move your body. Focus on your triceps instead of your chest.

Sit on an incline bench at 45 degrees and stretch arms fully to your sides. Supinate hands until you can’t anymore, so your arms are facing away from each other. Curl up, focusing on the deep stretch.

ex.note: Set yourself up as if you were doing a reverse grip pull down; focus on curling the weight down. Use your biceps, avoiding using your back.
Shift hips back to stretch glutes too; focus on hamstrings. Slightly bend knees
Don’t lock out; control weight. Place feet lower to feel quads and higher to feel hamstrings
Feel full stretch in glutes and hamstrings and curl up using same muscles. Load by hugging a plate or holding a bar behind neck
Lean back; stretch fully. End with partials
Bottom half ONLY; roll ankles. End with 30 second static stretch
Start with knee raises, then progress. Keep legs straight and avoid cheating with hips. Fully stretch abs at bottom

ss.note: Heavy but controlled. Lean forward for chest emphasis, find comfortable elbow position, and fully stretch. Don’t lock out
Integrated partials. Use 30 degree reverse grip, control eccentric. End with static stretch
